If you’re looking around **Sunderland**, I’d start with the Royal Kennel Club’s puppy listings rather than buying from a generic classified ad. Its current Staffordshire Bull Terrier search shows a **blue litter in Newcastle**, with both parents having at least one recorded health test. That listing is worth investigating, but the KC itself stresses that buyers still need to vet breeders independently. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com) [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-an-assured-breeder/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

There’s also a **North Eastern Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club** listed by the breed community, whose puppy-coordinator contact can be useful for finding established local breeders. [Staffordshire Bull Terrier Society](https://www.scsbts.com/sbt-welfare-and-rescue/buying-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

### What I'd ask the breeder

For a Staffy, don't settle for “both parents are health checked.” Ask to **see the actual certificates/results** for:

- **HC-HSF4-2 (hereditary cataracts)** DNA test.
- **L-2-HGA** DNA test.
- **Eye examination**, including litter eye screening before puppies leave.
- **Elbow dysplasia** screening.
- The parents' **KC registration details and health-test results**. These are among the breed-specific tests recommended by the Royal Kennel Club. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/BreedSpecificRequirements?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- The parents' **inbreeding coefficient**, and ask whether there are known health problems in their lines.

I'd also ask:

1. **Can I see the puppy with its mother and the rest of the litter at your home?**
2. **How old is the mother, and how many litters has she had?**
3. **Can I meet the father, or see his health certificates if he doesn't live there?**
4. **Why did you choose this particular mating?**
5. **What socialisation have the puppies had—children, household noises, other dogs, handling, car journeys?**
6. **What food are they eating and what routine are they used to?**
7. **Will the puppy be microchipped, vaccinated and wormed before collection?**
8. **What paperwork comes with the puppy?**
9. **What happens if I develop a problem after taking the puppy home? Will you take the dog back?**
10. **Can I speak to previous puppy owners?**

### One important point about “blue”

Don't let the colour become the main selling point. A blue Staffy can be perfectly healthy, but **colour does not tell you whether the breeder is responsible or whether the puppy's parents have been properly health tested**. The Royal Kennel Club's breed guidance puts substantial emphasis on genetic and clinical health screening. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

I'd also be wary of adverts using phrases such as **“rare blue,” “micro blue,” “XXL,” “champion bloodline”** or charging a large premium principally because of colour. Look at the parents, health evidence and breeding practices rather than the marketing.

**Before paying a deposit**, visit in person, see the mother interacting with the litter, check the paperwork yourself, and don't allow a seller to pressure you into transferring money because “someone else is coming to collect.”
